findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.8, redundant restatement, applied to the repeated question.
findings.diagnosis: The repetition is deliberate and it is the sentence's hinge: the chapters take up a question, and the first of them takes up a further question. Without the second the clause reads as though the chapters take up a capability, what civilizations can measure, rather than an open problem about it. The comma before and therefore also separates two consequences of the same question, so the second lands as an inference rather than as a second item in a list. This is the volume's only chapter transition that names the next chapter's subject as a question, which is what Chapter Seven then argues at length.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-02 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required, and this section is worth recording precisely because almost nothing happened to it. It carries a five-item list, two one-line fragments, an anaphoric four-part denial, and the protected phrase the work has begun in fragments, all of which are constructions the pass removed elsewhere in the volume. Set as an italic display block, they survived untouched. That is the third piece of evidence in this re-render that the pass's interventions tracked format rather than principle: it rewrote running prose and left display matter alone.
